Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot with complaints of right knee pain, swelling, and
reduced range of motion. Over eight visits, care consisted of conservative management including anti-inflammatory
medication, a structured physical therapy program, activity modification, and bracing during ambulation. Initial
examination showed mild effsuion and tendenress along the medial joint line, with pain reproduced on flexion beyond
ninety degrees, findings that are consistent with the mechanism of injury described. Ligamentous stability testing and
neuorvascular examination were within normal limits. The patient reports no prior injury or treatment involving this
knee. Treatment progressed in a typical pattern, with pain and swelling steadily decreasing and visit frequency
tapering as functional strength and mobility improved. Billed services correspond to the visits documented, with no
duplicate or repeated charges identified. Patient was discharged to a self-directed home execrise program with
instructions to return if symptoms recur.
